description: We're Software Engineering Technology (AI) students from Centennial College, and our studies makes us fit for this challenge: machine learning and unsupervised learning to find patterns in satellite data, big data tools for large NASA datasets, and full-stack and mobile development (React, Node.js) to ship a working app. We've also built a multi-agent AI assistant with LLMs and ChromaDB. We're looking for a designer or someone with audio or science experience to round out the team.
summary: Baseline is health monitoring software for a crew on a long mission, built for the moment Earth can't help in time. On a Mars mission a message to the ground takes about 3 to 22 minutes each way, so the crew has to notice and act on a problem themselves. Baseline compares each astronaut with their own normal, not a population average. It explains what is off in plain words and gives the first step to take. In an emergency it alerts every crew tablet with the person's location and readings, and talks the responder through a step-by-step guide. During a spacewalk it warns the crew before the astronaut has to ask. It works fully offline, including voice control.
details:
WHAT IT DOES
Personal baselines: every reading (heart and breathing, sleep, mind, eyes, blood sugar, kidneys and fluids, bone and muscle, temperature, radiation) is scored against that astronaut's own recent normal, so a slow drift is flagged before it becomes an emergency.
Plain-language flags: each flag says what changed, why it matters in space, and the first step of the plan. Each reading names the device it would come from, for example the CSA Bio-Monitor shirt for pulse and breathing.
"Are you OK?" check: when readings turn serious, the astronaut's own tablet asks first. If they don't answer, or say they need help, every crew tablet is alerted.
Crew alert: who needs help, where they are, their key readings, whether they answered, and how long a reply from Earth takes. A responder can open the patient's 3D body view and all their readings.
Emergency guide: a step-by-step, timed guide for an unresponsive crewmate, based on the DGLRM / ESAM-SMG guideline for CPR in microgravity (Hinkelbein et al., 2020). It is read aloud, works by voice, and is labelled a draft protocol, not clinically reviewed.
Incident report: a timestamped record of the emergency (detection, readings at start and end, every guide step, responder, outcome, follow-up) that can be printed, saved as PDF, or opened as an email draft to the flight surgeon. If the link to Earth is down, it waits in the outbox.
Spacewalk (EVA) mode: suit pressure, CO2, oxygen time at the current effort, heart rate and body temperature at the top of every tablet. A warning is spoken at the first abnormal reading and the crew is alerted at a critical one, before the astronaut has to ask. If suit data stops arriving, Baseline says the readings are no longer live and warns the crew.
Offline procedure search: questions such as "what do I do for a fever?" are answered by searching the on-board plans and quoting them word for word with their source. Nothing is generated, so nothing can be invented.
Offline voice: "Baseline, how am I doing?", "crewmate down", "I'm going", "next". Speech recognition runs on the tablet with OpenAI's Whisper model, so no audio leaves the spacecraft, and the crew can answer while Baseline is still talking.
Crew simulator: real astronaut health data is protected, so the prototype runs on simulated crew data, with a built-in simulator for scenarios (collapse, fever, low oxygen, suit faults).

HOW IT WORKS
One web page that runs offline in any tablet, phone or laptop browser. Tablets talk over the local network; data is stored on the tablet (SQLite in WebAssembly). 3D body: three.js. Voice: Whisper tiny in the browser through transformers.js and ONNX Runtime Web. Health logic is fixed, readable rules, not a black-box model, so every alert can be explained and tested.

QUALITY
201 automated checks across five test suites. Voice benchmark: 43 of 56 recorded test phrases understood (synthetic voices); real-voice testing is next.

HONEST LIMITS
Simulated data only. Thresholds are prototype starting values, not clinically validated. The CPR guide is a draft that needs review by a flight surgeon.

TOOLS
HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python, Node.js with Puppeteer (tests), three.js, sql.js, transformers.js, ONNX Runtime Web, Whisper.

SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) DISCLOSURE
Parts of the code, tests and documentation were generated with Claude (Anthropic), then run, reviewed and tested by Team TechTribe. No SI makes health decisions in Baseline.
